title.narrative: ILO/ITC Trade for jobs Phase 1 - Trade for jobs

description.narrative:
Uganda has experienced steady economic growth, yet this has not translated into sufficient productive employment or broad-based prosperity. Persistent underemployment, informality, and weak trade performance continue to limit opportunities, particularly for women and youth. The programme seeks to address these systemic constraints by strengthening the market systems in high-potential sectors - dairy and tourism - to enable trade-driven, inclusive and sustainable job creation.
The objective of this intervention is to implement an 18-month inception phase that will establish the foundations for the full implementation of the Trade for Jobs Uganda programme (Phase II).
The Trade for Jobs Uganda programme is a joint initiative of the International Labour Organization (ILO) and the International Trade Centre (ITC), funded by Sida.
Its stated objective is: The project will create more and better jobs and increased incomes for women and men living in poverty in Uganda, by unlocking trade and micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) growth.
Both the inception phase (phase 1) and the phase 2 will focus on the dairy and tourism sectors, which an extensive study has identified as high-potential areas for trade-driven job creation and income growth. By the end of the interventions, the programme intends to achieve the following changes for its target beneficiaries:
- Strengthened regional and global trade of dairy products and tourism services, with a focus on micro enterprises and SMEs.
- Support for private sector development in both the dairy and the tourism sector, including value addition, diversification, enhanced competitiveness, and an improved business environment.
- Engagement with Swedish companies to leverage expertise, services, products, and private investment for local sector growth.
The project will apply a Market Systems Development (MSD) approach, which emphasizes local ownership, systemic change, and long-term sustainability. Its unique contribution lies in leveraging trade as a driver of decent job creation, combining ILOs expertise in decent work with ITCs experience in trade and SME competitiveness.
Dairy Sector Objective
By the end of the program, the dairy sector is expected to:
- Boost farm-level productivity, sales, and incomes through improved animal health, genetics, feed, and access to finance.
- Strengthen milk collection centres (MCCs) by enhancing technical and organizational capacities and adopting quality-based payment systems, thereby increasing sales, incomes, and job creation.
- Improve regulation, sector coordination, and export promotion to diversify markets and increase trade of competitive dairy products (e.g., UHT milk, yoghurt, powdered milk).
The intended change is that micro and smallholder dairy producers, MCCs, processors, and exporters will increase productivity and competitiveness, leading to higher incomes and more decent jobs.
Tourism Sector Objective
By the end of the program, the tourism sector is expected to:
- Enhance international and regional market access for MSMEs by improving digital visibility, buyer linkages, and coordinated destination promotion.
- Strengthen the tourism skills system so that it better meets market needs, formalises employment, and increases decent job creation.
- Improve governance and regulation to support MSME formalisation and growth, creating an enabling environment for inclusive trade and job opportunities
The intended change is that tourism MSMEs particularly those employing women and youth will gain better access to high-value markets, improve service quality, and expand decent employment opportunities.
While these objectives provide direction for both the inception phase and Phase 2, the activities undertaken in each phase will differ.
Key priorities and expected achievements of the inception phase
The proposed support covers Trade for Jobs Uganda the programmes initial inception phase (Phase 1), to be implemented over a period of 18 months. This phase is envisaged to be followed by a full-scale implementation phase (Phase 2). However, Phase 2 remains non-committal at this stage and will be subject to a separate appraisal and decision process. Together, Phases 1 and 2 are expected to span a total period of approximately five years.
The objective of the inception phase is to establish the institutional, strategic and operational foundations for programme implementation. The inception phase will focus on the following key priorities:
- Establishing programme structures, including the recruitment and capacity development of staff, and the formation of a Project Steering Committee.
- Undertaking in-depth analysis and strategic planning, including revision of the Theory of Change, risk register and results framework, and development of systems for monitoring, learning and results measurement (MRM)
- Organising a Sidaproject review meeting to jointly review, analyse and validate the projects strategic direction and feasibility.
- Facilitating partner and donor coordination, in close collaboration with relevant Ugandan institutions, private sector actors, development partners and Swedish companies.
- Mapping and engaging Swedish companies to identify opportunities for collaboration within the programme framework.
- Conducting gender, environmental and climate analyses, and developing a communication and knowledge management plan.
- Designing and testing pilot interventions in the two selected sectors dairy and tourism to trial models and partnerships that can be scaled up during the subsequent implementation phase.
